findings.hypothesis: A large proportion of orders never progress from created to confirmed (417,569 lost; conversion 0.3548). This is a system-level funnel gap worth prioritizing for remediation rather than a small edge-case.
findings.confirm_via: Run an experiment that targets the full created cohort with a lightweight confirmation nudge (A/B test sending an in-app/email nudge immediately after creation) and measure lift in confirmed count and conversion_from_previous versus control.

findings.hypothesis: Documented user and artifact reasons explain a substantial but incomplete portion of the top gap (user_total: 199417 + artifact_total: 42107 = explained portion). A meaningful remainder of the 417,569 loss (i.e., ~176k) is unexplained by reason clusters and likely due to other operational or UX factors.
findings.confirm_via: Add an experimented telemetry/mandatory reason capture for a representative sample of created orders (force a lightweight reason selection or passive event capture) to shrink the unexplained bucket and validate which new reason(s) account for the remaining ~176k loss.

findings.hypothesis: Orders labeled rx_gated have materially lower confirmation rate (rate: 0.3002) than non_rx orders (rate: 0.3904); because rx_gated is large (entered: 255293) it accounts for a big share of the top gap. This is a correlation that suggests consultation-related friction is a major contributor to the unexplained loss.
findings.confirm_via: Run a controlled experiment that reduces friction for rx_gated orders (e.g., prioritized clinician callbacks, express consultation slots, or automated triage) and measure change in rx_gated conversion (converted and rate) versus control; if conversion increases toward non_rx levels, consultation friction is causal.
